title: Macaulay Education Policy Impact in Bengal
subtitle: Macaulay’s 1835 Minute urged government support for European learning through English; Bentinck’s resolution followed in March.
summary: On 2 February 1835, Thomas Babington Macaulay, as president of the General Committee of Public Instruction, submitted a Minute arguing that the government’s education funds should promote European literature and science through English. Governor-General William Bentinck’s resolution of 7 March 1835 endorsed that direction. The Minute was an influential intervention in a wider dispute over education funding and language; it was not itself an act abolishing all indigenous or vernacular education. The available event sources do not document the policy’s specific implementation and effects in Bengal.
heroTagline: An education policy debate whose Bengal effects require closer local evidence.
whyItMatters: The Minute and Bentinck’s resolution helped redirect colonial education policy toward English-language instruction and European knowledge, while leaving contested questions about vernacular learning and access. Because this chapter promises impact in Bengal, it needs Bengal-specific evidence on institutions, implementation, and social consequences that the current general sources do not supply.

The available sources do not establish the policy’s local effects across Bengal.
